pr_title: Address some edge cases in EncoderNLS.GetBytes draining logic
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33817.

There were two edge cases that weren't handled properly in the `EncoderNLS.GetBytes` draining logic. The first - as originally reported in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/415#issuecomment-601267431 - was triggered when a call to `EncoderNLS.GetBytes` was given a buffer which ended in a high surrogate character, and where the next call to `EncoderNLS.GetBytes` would not provide the low surrogate character at the start of the new input buffer.

The second edge case occurred where the first call to `EncoderNLS.GetBytes` ended with a high surrogate character, the second call began with the low surrogate character, _and_ the corresponding supplementary code point was not representable in the target encoding.

This fix addresses both edge cases. This code path is shared by `EncoderNLS.Convert`, so no separate fix was needed for that routine. The unit tests cover both `GetBytes` and `Convert` just to be safe.

issue_context.title: UTF8 encoder returns different results if Convert is called only once or multiple times with the same source data
comments:
I couldn't add an area label to this Issue.

Checkout [this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md) page to find out which area owner to ping, or please add exactly one area label to help train me in the future.
@GrabYourPitchforks I think this was intentional behavior for net core. right?

Need to look at it a bit closer. OP originally reported at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/415#issuecomment-601267431 but the repro code there was truncated so I wasn't able to test it locally.

Bug is at the following location in _EncoderNLS.cs_. This block of code should set `_charLeftOver = default;` upon execution, just like all the other cases in the switch statement which precedes it.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/cd09cd3999b862360f4f9811f243a2baabb330f9/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Text/EncoderNLS.cs#L397-L400

I've also marked this as _servicing-consider_ for v3.x.
@GrabYourPitchforks I am not sure this will meet the servicing bar.

I'm not sure either, but I wanted to at least have the discussion. This could possibly lead to data corruption of the output, but _only if_ the original input was also corrupted through the presence of a standalone unpaired surrogate. Given the "garbage-in/garbage-out" behavior it's certainly less severe than the other UTF-8 issues we've backported.
